question: Which US common stocks, listed today or delisted, met the research pool's floor often enough in 2005 to mid-2025 to belong to a wider universe that no rule has seen? (Engineering check: lists and counts only, no returns.)
next_step: Each shard becomes a frozen dataset (builder 'universe', daily history from 1995) registered separately. The weekly V3 pattern, once its definition is frozen from the user's labels, is tested on these unseen stocks against same-day random stocks from the same shard.
notes: User decision 2026-10-14: widen the stock pool so the fixed weekly V3 pattern has enough signals (the strict definition gives about 6 a year in the 1,228-stock universe) and so the final test uses stocks no rule has seen.

Candidates: EODHD exchange-symbol-list US, listed and delisted, Type 'Common Stock' on NYSE, NASDAQ, AMEX, NYSE MKT or NYSE ARCA (the primary-exchange filter of services/scanner/audit_eodhd.py). Tickers present in both lists are left out, because a reused ticker can join two companies' prices; the 1,228 stocks of universe-1985-v1 are left out.

Kept: at least 60 sessions from 2005-01-01 to 2025-06-30 with adjusted close >= $5 and adjusted close x volume >= $10M (the research pool floor). Downloads use three attempts each and four parallel requests to stay inside the provider's rate limit.
Passed if at most 10% of downloads fail and at least 1,000 stocks are kept. The lists and counts are reported whatever they show; no price result is looked at.
